title: Differential Roles of hsa-miR-124-3p and hsa-miR-124-5p in Primary Tumors and Peritoneal Metastases of Ovarian Cancer: Associations with Potential Targets
content: This study aimed to investigate potential interactions of hsa-miR-124-3p and hsa-miR-124-5p with their predicted targets and regulatory long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in primary epithelial ovarian tumors and peritoneal metastases. Candidate selection combined public Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets, ENCORI records, and HTA 2.0 microarray screening. Expression level of two miR-124 strands, seven target mRNAs (ANAPC1, FKBP14, GK5, IL15RA, PARP14, SNAI2, TRAF3), lncRNAs GAS5, MAGI2-AS3, MEG3, and some epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers was analyzed by extensive RT-qPCR profiling. A representative clinical cohort including 119 primary tumors (patients with and without metastases) and 40 peritoneal metastases were used. Relative to histologically normal tissues, primary tumors exhibited altered expression of miR-124-3p, miR-124-5p, and EMT-associated genes, alongside negative correlations between both miR-124 strands and some predicted mRNA and lncRNA targets. Functional assays using hsa-miR-124-3p and hsa-miR-124-5p mimics in SKOV3 and OVCAR3 cells confirmed several regulatory interactions, such as the GAS5/hsa-miR-124-3p(-5p)/ANAPC1 axis. Notably, hsa-miR-124-5p levels were significantly elevated in peritoneal macrometastases in the majority of paired cases (25/34, p = 0.0036), whereas hsa-miR-124-3p levels did not show significant changes (p &gt; 0.05). Collectively, our results support the differential involvement of miR-124 strands and their targets in peritoneal metastasis, which requires further mechanistic investigation.
